newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SUB NIGEL RISES ON SPECULATION OF BUYS.
newsitem.headline: SUB NIGEL RISES ON SPECULATION OF BUYS.

text.p: Shares in South Africa's Sub Nigel Gold Mining Co Ltd continued to rise on Thursday on speculation that a planned purchase of information businesses may be immiment, dealers said.
By 0900 GMT Sub Nigel shares were up nearly 14 percent or nine cents to 74 cents, building on its five cent gain on Wednesday. Volumes were moderate at nearly 158,000 shares.

Dealers said that an announcement on Wednesday that the firm would increase its share capital and was converting some of its preference shares into ordinary shares may mean there was an acquisition in the pipeline.
"There seems to be a lot of small trades being done for private clients which points to speculative trade. They could be buying something," one dealer said.

Sub-Nigel said on May 12 that following inconclusive talks on the disposal of its mining interests it was considering forming a new firm Listco which would buy businesses in the information technology sector.
It also planned to move its listing to the Johannesburg Stock Exchange electrical and electronics sector.
On Wednesday it said it anticiapted making a further announcement relating to these acquisitions.
It also said it had received shareholder approval to increase the company's authorised share capital by creating 70 million convertible preference shares of one cent each.

At the same time it had also been given the nod to convert the 70 million preference shares into 70 million ordinary shares of no par value so that the authorised share capital of Sub Nigel now comprises 100 million ordinary shares of no par value.
The authorised but unissued share capital of the company would remain under the directors' control until the next annual general meeting.
